notes.note: The pronoun I here and throughout this chapter refers to Paul. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state this explicitly. Alternate translation: [I, Paul, urge]

The pronouns you and your here and throughout most of this chapter are plural and refer to the believers in Rome to whom Paul wrote this letter. If it would be helpful in your language, you could say this explicitly. Alternate translation: [you believers … your … your]

The word Therefore indicates that what follows is a logical conclusion. Here, therefore indicates that what follows in the rest of this letter is what Paul wants his readers to do in response to what he has written in chapters 1–11. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a fuller expression. Alternate translation: [Since everything I have said is true, I urge you]

Here, the lowly ones could refer to: (1) people who are poor or are not respected by society. Alternate translation: [accepting people who do not seem important]; (2) doings things that people think are humiliating or unimportant. Alternate translation: [accepting the lowly tasks]

verses.text: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.

xrefs.text: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.
Make sure that no one repays evil for evil. Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people.
Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.
But I tell you not to resist an evil person. If someone slaps you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also;
We want to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift.

Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable— if anything is excellent or praiseworthy— think on these things.
Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
keeping a clear conscience, so that those who slander you may be put to shame by your good behavior in Christ.

notes.quote: μηδενὶ κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἀποδιδόντες, προνοούμενοι καλὰ ἐνώπιον πάντων ἀνθρώπων
notes.note: Paul is using statements to give commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a more natural form for commands. Alternate translation: [repay no one evil for evil; give careful thought to good things in the sight of all men]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of evil, thought, and sight, you could express the ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [evil things for evil things; thinking carefully about … as seen by]

Here Paul uses paying back to refer to doing something evil to someone in response to the evil that person has done. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [doing something evil to no one for the evil that person has done to you]

Here Paul uses sight to refer to what people mentally perceive. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [do things that all men perceive to be good]
Although the term men is masculine, Paul is using the word here in a generic sense that includes both men and women. Alternate translation: [all people]

verses.text: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.

xrefs.text: Pursue peace with everyone, as well as holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.
Finally, brothers, rejoice! Aim for perfect harmony, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every evil practice.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.
Deceit is in the hearts of those who devise evil, but the counselors of peace have joy.

notes.note: Alternate translation: [so far as it depends on you] or [as much as it is up to you]
Paul is using a statement to give a command. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a more natural form for commands. Alternate translation: [live at peace with all men]
Although the term men is masculine, Paul is using the word here in a generic sense that includes both men and women. Alternate translation: [all people]

verses.text: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”

xrefs.text: Vengeance is Mine; I will repay. In due time their foot will slip; for their day of disaster is near, and their doom is coming quickly.”
For we know Him who said, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge His people.”
Do not say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”
Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.
Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
and no one should ever violate or exploit his brother in this regard, because the Lord will avenge all such acts, as we have already told you and solemnly warned you.
Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against any of your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.

notes.note: Paul is using a statement to give a command. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a more natural form for commands. Alternate translation: [do not avenge yourselves]
Here, wrath refers to God’s punishment. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [give way to God’s punishment]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of wrath and vengeance, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [to God being wrathful … I will avenge]

For indicates that what follows this word explains what came before it. Here, for indicates that what follows is the reason why what Paul said in the previous clause is true. Use a natural way in your language for indicating a reason. You may need to start a new sentence, as in the UST. Alternate translation: [This is due to the fact that]
See how you translated the similar phrase in 1:17.

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Moses wrote this quotation. Alternate translation: [Moses wrote]

notes.quote: ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις; ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω, λέγει Κύριος
notes.note: This sentence is a quotation of Deuteronomy 32:35. It may be helpful to your readers to indicate this by setting off all of this material with quotation marks or with whatever punctuation or convention your language uses to indicate a quotation.

notes.quote: ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις; ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω, λέγει Κύριος
notes.note: If the direct quotation inside a direct quotation would be confusing in your language, you could translate the second direct quotation as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [The Lord says that vengeance is for him; he will repay.]

These two phrases mean basically the same thing and emphasize that God will avenge his people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could combine the phrases into one. Alternate translation: [I will certainly avenge you]

Here Moses quotes God using repay to refer to appropriately punishing someone as if the punishment were reciprocal payment for that person’s deeds. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will appropriately punish]

Moses quotes God leaving out some of the words that a sentence would need in many languages to be complete. If it would be helpful in your language, you could supply these words from the context. Alternate translation: [will repay them]

named.name: LORD
named.brief: Names or title used to refer to God

verses.text: On the contrary, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”

xrefs.text: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
If you encounter your enemy’s stray ox or donkey, you must return it to him.
“Do not kill them,” he replied. “Would you kill those you have captured with your own sword or bow? Set food and water before them, that they may eat and drink and then return to their master.”
When David had finished saying these things, Saul called back, “Is that your voice, David my son?” Then Saul wept aloud
Then Saul replied, “I have sinned. Come back, David my son. I will never harm you again, because today you considered my life precious. I have played the fool and have committed a grave error!”
Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm. For love is as strong as death, its jealousy as unrelenting as Sheol. Its sparks are fiery flames, the fiercest blaze of all.

notes.note: But here indicates that what follows is a quotation from an Old Testament book (Proverbs 25:21–22). If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a comparable phrase that indicates that Paul is quoting from an important text. Alternate translation: [But, God says in the Scriptures,]

notes.quote: ἐὰν πεινᾷ ὁ ἐχθρός σου, ψώμιζε αὐτόν; ἐὰν διψᾷ, πότιζε αὐτόν; τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν, ἄνθρακας πυρὸς σωρεύσεις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ
notes.note: This sentence is a quotation of Proverbs 25:21–22. It may be helpful to your readers to indicate this by setting off all of this material with quotation marks or with whatever punctuation or convention your language uses to indicate a quotation.
Here the pronouns your and you are singular and addressed as though to one person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use plural forms here.

For indicates that what follows this word explains what came before it. Here, For indicates that what follows is the reason why what was said in the previous sentence is true. Use a natural way in your language for indicating a reason. Alternate translation: [This is due to the fact that]

notes.quote: ἄνθρακας πυρὸς σωρεύσεις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ
notes.note: This clause is an idiom. It could refer to: (1) a person feeling shame as a result of being helped by someone whom that person had harmed. Alternate translation: [you will make the person who harmed you feel badly about how he has mistreated you]; (2) God very severely punishing the person who is being helped. Alternate translation: [you will give God a reason to judge him more harshly]

verses.text: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

xrefs.text: Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.
But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.

notes.quote: μὴ νικῶ ὑπὸ τοῦ κακοῦ, ἀλλὰ νίκα ἐν τῷ ἀγαθῷ τὸ κακόν
notes.note: Paul describes evil as if it were a person who could conquer someone or be conquered by someone. He is referring to someone doing evil in response to someone doing evil to that person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Do not let evil cause you to do evil, but use good to prevent evil from influencing you]

notes.quote: τοῦ κακοῦ & τῷ ἀγαθῷ τὸ κακόν
notes.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of evil and good, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [evil things … evil things … good things]
If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Do not let evil overcome you]
